summary:
AstroVital
A visual tool designed to help astronauts assess their own health during space missions and determine the appropriate course of action.

Proposal for the Create Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts on Space Missions challenge at NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.
details:
AstroVital — Project Description

AstroVital is a space health monitoring platform designed to help astronauts assess their health, understand potential medical risks, and make informed decisions during space missions.

The platform provides an integrated visual health monitoring experience that combines vital sign tracking, clinical alerts, assisted diagnostics, and a realistic 3D anatomical digital twin. Astronauts can monitor their physiological indicators, explore different anatomical systems, identify potential health concerns, and access contextual recommendations based on their mission environment.

How It Works

AstroVital organizes its functionality into several interconnected modules:

  • Health Monitoring: Tracks vital signs and displays historical trends, allowing astronauts to monitor changes in their physiological condition.
  • Clinical Diagnostics: Provides simulated assisted diagnostic capabilities to help interpret health indicators and identify potential warning signs.
  • 3D Anatomical Digital Twin: Features an interactive human anatomical model based on BodyParts3D, allowing astronauts to explore the skin, organ systems, skeletal structures, and clinically relevant anatomical regions.
  • Clinical Alerts: Uses configurable clinical thresholds to classify health conditions into nominal, caution, and critical categories.
  • Environmental and Mission Context: Adapts clinical rules according to the astronaut's location, considering different environments such as spacecraft, space stations, lunar and Martian bases, rovers, and Earth.
  • Medical Support and Wellbeing: Integrates medical kit information, environmental life-support considerations, and daily mission recommendations.

Benefits and Intended Impact

Long-duration space missions expose astronauts to unique physiological and environmental challenges. Limited access to immediate medical assistance makes continuous health monitoring and clear decision-support tools particularly important.

AstroVital aims to:

  • Improve astronauts' awareness of their own physiological condition.
  • Facilitate the early identification of potentially concerning health changes.
  • Make complex anatomical and physiological information easier to understand through interactive visualization.
  • Support informed health-related decisions in environments with limited medical resources.
  • Provide a modular foundation for future integration with real medical sensors and spacecraft health-monitoring systems.

Our intended impact is to contribute to safer and more sustainable human space exploration by making health information more accessible, understandable, and actionable for astronauts.

The architecture follows Clean Architecture, Vertical Slicing, and tactical Domain-Driven Design (DDD), promoting modularity, maintainability, and scalability.

The application can operate with Supabase integration or with in-memory adapters and demonstration data. No custom hardware is required for the current prototype.

Creativity and Innovation

AstroVital's main innovation lies in combining several traditionally separate healthcare concepts into a unified, interactive space-health platform.

Rather than presenting vital signs as isolated numbers or conventional charts, the platform connects physiological monitoring with a navigable 3D anatomical representation of the human body.

This digital twin allows astronauts to explore anatomical structures and access clinically relevant information through a visual interface. Combined with location-dependent clinical rules, this approach introduces an additional layer of contextual awareness to health monitoring.

Another distinctive aspect is the integration of space mission environments into the clinical rules system. Health thresholds and recommendations are designed to account for the differences between Earth, spacecraft, orbital stations, and extraterrestrial environments.

The result is a platform that combines medical visualization, contextual monitoring, and mission-oriented decision support in a single experience.

Factors Considered During Development

Several important factors guided the design and development of AstroVital:

  • Space mission constraints: Medical assistance and resources may be limited during long-duration missions.
  • Environmental variability: Physiological monitoring must account for the different conditions associated with spacecraft, orbital stations, and lunar or Martian environments.
  • Usability: Astronauts need clear visual information, intuitive navigation, and easily identifiable alert categories.
  • Anatomical accuracy: The 3D model uses BodyParts3D, an established anatomical resource, under its applicable licensing terms.
  • Data integrity and security: The architecture incorporates data validation and Supabase Row-Level Security.
  • Scalability: The modular architecture facilitates future integration with external sensors, additional diagnostic capabilities, and other mission systems.
  • Scientific responsibility: Clinical thresholds and diagnostic features are treated as configurable or simulated decision-support mechanisms, not as substitutes for validated medical procedures or professional medical judgment.
